subject: English
summaryPoints: Comprehensive synthesis of tenses: Simple Past (discrete finished actions), Past Continuous (past action in progress), Present Perfect (past action with present impact), and Present Perfect Continuous (action ongoing from past to present).
Past continuous narrative framing uses time clauses to set background scenes before main events occur in the simple past.
Present perfect continuous emphasizes the sustained effort or repetitive duration leading directly up to the current moment.

Phrasal verbs centered on 'cut' and 'do' include 'cut down on' (reduce intake), 'cut into' (slice or interrupt), 'cut off' (sever or disconnect), 'do away with' (abolish/eliminate), 'do over' (repeat/redo), 'do without' (manage in the absence of), and 'doze off' (fall asleep inadvertently).

Communicative discourse formulas express degrees of opinion ('In my opinion', 'I believe'), agreement ('I couldn't agree more', 'Definitely'), and polite disagreement ('I'm afraid I disagree', 'I'm not sure I agree').

Technological literacy texts examine the dual nature of computer technology and the internet: expanding global information and connectivity versus diminishing interpersonal skills and physical activity.

formulas.label: Tense Aspect Contrast Summary
formulas.expr: Simple Past: S + V2  |  Past Continuous: S + was/were + V-ing  |  Present Perfect: S + has/have + V3  |  Present Perfect Continuous: S + has/have + been + V-ing

formulas.label: Opinion Stating Expression Pattern
formulas.expr: In my opinion, / From my perspective, + [Complete Clause]  |  I think/believe that + [Complete Clause]

formulas.label: Polite Disagreement Formula
formulas.expr: I see your point, but...  |  I'm afraid I have to disagree with...  |  I am not sure that is entirely correct

examTip: In EUEE reading and narrative passages testing mixed tenses, identify the precise temporal relationship of events: use simple past for completed sequential actions, past continuous for background ongoing actions, and present perfect if the narrative transitions to impact the speaker in the present.

keyDefinitions.definition: A grammatical category that reflects how an action, event, or state, as denoted by a verb, extends or unfolds over time (simple, progressive, or perfect).
The functional purposes for which language is deployed in social discourse, such as stating opinions, agreeing, disagreeing, or asking clarification.
A global computer network facilitating vast data transmission, multimedia communication, online interaction, and shared information services.
Mental agility or physical readiness and skill in performing tasks, particularly with the hands.
